title: Parallel Axiom
summary: Playfair's Axiom selects Euclidean geometry by asserting existence and uniqueness of a parallel through an external point.
statements: Given a line ℓ and a point P not on ℓ, there is exactly one line through P that is parallel to ℓ.

historicalContext.title: From Euclid's fifth postulate to Playfair
paragraphs: Euclid's fifth postulate was phrased using a transversal: if the interior angles on one side total less than two right angles, the two lines meet on that side. John Playfair later popularized the equivalent formulation now bearing his name: through an external point there is at most one parallel to a given line.

The other axioms can establish the existence of at least one parallel through an external point, so Playfair's historical at-most-one statement becomes exactly one. This app states exactly one directly to keep the foundation self-contained.

Centuries of attempts to derive the fifth postulate from the other axioms ultimately led to non-Euclidean geometry, where parallel behavior is different. Playfair's Axiom is therefore the deliberate assumption that selects Euclidean geometry here.

whatItEnables: Once a constructed line through P is proved parallel to ℓ, uniqueness identifies it with the parallel supplied by the axiom. This is the specifically Euclidean step in later parallel-line theorems.
